clue.text: Working in shed, hence best in private

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, so the letters of the following words are kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone busy in the garden shed thinks it is best to keep their work out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like the activity going on in the shed, but it signals that IN SHED HENCE BEST is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done backstage or out of public view is done secretly, privately, away from the audience.

clue.text: Convert boring quiet nuns? An urgent issue

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters of the three following words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Whether dull, silent nuns could be converted is posed as a pressing question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convert' reads as a religious conversion of the nuns, but it tells you to rearrange BORING QUIET NUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a matter that is hotly debated and demands immediate attention is a pressing, urgent issue.

clue.text: Spy usually has one name, right?

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name or title

explanation.surface: A question about whether a spy goes by a single name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has one name' tempts you toward aliases; the definition is the whole opening phrase, the agent's controller.
explanation.definitionFit: In espionage, the officer who runs and directs an agent is that agent's controller, something nearly every spy has.

clue.text: Two common answers given in recess

parts.note: two everyday replies to a question are no and OK
two everyday replies to a question are no and OK

explanation.surface: Two everyday replies are offered during a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a recess is a small alcove or corner set into a wall or room.

clue.text: Figure left in Lincoln characterising a sound principle

parts.note: a figure is a number, here ten

indicators.note: in says the letter for left is placed inside the president's short name

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's familiar name

explanation.surface: A number written on the left of a Lincoln portrait somehow describes a sound principle.
explanation.walkthrough: ABE is Abraham Lincoln, the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle that is sound can be defended and maintained in argument, which is what describes a defensible position.

clue.text: Take advantage of heroic achievement

definitions.meaning: a verb: to use someone or something unfairly for one's own gain
a noun: a bold or daring feat

explanation.surface: Cashing in on a hero's great deed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning to make unfair use of and a noun meaning a daring deed.

clue.text: Curtail section of programme

definitions.meaning: a verb: to trim or cut short
a noun: a short extract shown from a film or broadcast

explanation.surface: An editor cutting short a piece of a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to trim something and a short excerpt taken from a film or television show.

clue.text: Teachers' group action is a daft one

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union
an action is a lawsuit, a legal case

explanation.surface: A teachers' union deciding that some protest is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was the UK's National Union of Teachers; an action in law is a case brought to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a crazy or foolish person is called this in colloquial British English.

clue.text: It's untrue ferret scampers around in bins, say

indicators.note: the ferret running about wildly signals that the letters of the preceding words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A denial that a ferret is darting about inside the rubbish bins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scampers around' looks like the ferret's movement, but it is the anagram signal; 'bins, say' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Bins are an example of the fixtures placed along roads, alongside benches, bollards and lamp posts.

clue.text: Summary in a poor state

definitions.meaning: a noun: a brief account of the main points

explanation.surface: A report summarising something in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated word means both a quick summary of the facts and, as an adjective, shabby or worn out.

clue.text: Playwright Oscar's detained, giving needle

indicators.note: detained means held inside, so the playwright's name keeps the letter within it

parts.note: Harold Pinter was a British playwright
Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: Playwright Oscar Wilde is held in custody and given a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playwright Oscar' suggests Wilde, but the playwright is Pinter and Oscar is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a needle on a dial or gauge is the indicator that shows the reading.

clue.text: Unemployed star on radio

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard, not seen, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a star is a celebrity or idol

explanation.surface: A star presenter who has lost their job turns up on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone not working or without a job is inactive.

clue.text: Man at top of order?

parts.note: a monastic order is headed by its senior monk, not a boss at the top of a list or a top-order batsman

explanation.surface: A question about who sits at the head of some ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' suggests a list or a batting order; the order here is a religious community.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an abbey of monks is the man in charge of that religious order's house.

clue.text: Mist in west London area reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the place name is given by how it sounds

parts.note: Hayes is a district in the London Borough of Hillingdon, in west London

explanation.surface: Fog is reported over a district in west London.
explanation.walkthrough: HAYES is a suburb in west London, near Heathrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thin mist or fog blurs the air.

clue.text: Fare in Texan city put up half-heartedly

indicators.note: half the heart goes: of the doubled middle letters of the turned city, one is dropped
in a down clue, put up means the city's name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Dallas is a major city in Texas

explanation.surface: Food served in a Texas city, put on the table without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns DALLAS into SALLAD; 'half-heartedly' drops one of its two central Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare means food, and a dish of raw leaves and vegetables is one kind of food.

clue.text: Husband with a young dog not raised in fortunate way

indicators.note: not says the letters for raised are removed from the young dog

parts.note: a young dog is a puppy
raised means up

explanation.surface: A husband with a puppy that was not brought up well is somehow lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not raised' removes UP from PUPPY, leaving PPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone fortunate or lucky is in a favourable, pleasant situation.

clue.text: Bachelor, in place of car, gets American rubbish

indicators.note: in says the letter for bachelor goes inside the car's building

parts.note: a garage is where a car is kept

explanation.surface: A single man keeps junk in his garage instead of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place of' looks like substitution, but 'in' alone is the container signal and 'place of car' is GARAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage this is the everyday word for household waste or trash.

clue.text: Note stout fellow catching a criminal

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the beer and fellow letters enclose the single letter

parts.note: stout is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A sturdy chap writes a note while apprehending a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: TEA LEAF is Cockney rhyming slang for thief; 'stout' is the beer, not 'fat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: the phrase rhymes with thief, so in London slang it names a criminal who steals.

clue.text: Posh doctor with anger giving offence

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in 'U and non-U' usage
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: An upper-class doctor's fury causes offence.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class, posh, comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' language debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to take this is to take offence, feeling resentment at a slight.

clue.text: Reserve rental accommodation in small publication

parts.note: to reserve is to book
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: Booking a holiday rental through a little brochure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thin bound pamphlet is a small printed publication.

clue.text: A ruse devised on road heading north in huge region

indicators.note: something devised is invented or made up, so the letters of the trick are reworked
in a down clue, heading north means the road is read upwards

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A trick planned on a road leading north into a vast area.
explanation.walkthrough: A RUSE rearranged gives EURAS; the A1 (AI) is a major British trunk road, turned to give IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The combined landmass of Europe and Asia is a huge geographical region.

clue.text: Where one might find masthead in theory

definitions.meaning: a newspaper's title banner is printed on its front page sheet
an adverbial phrase: theoretically, though not in practice

explanation.surface: Where a ship's masthead might be found in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masthead' suggests a sailing ship; it is the newspaper's title banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that works on the page or in principle may not work in reality.

clue.text: Work after month to find sea creature

indicators.note: after says the work comes later than the month in the answer

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A composer's work, written after a certain month, leads to finding a sea animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-armed cephalopod is a sea creature.

clue.text: Religious leader holding mass before two in Latin community of old

indicators.note: before says the leader piece precedes the numeral
holding means containing, so the leader's title has the letter inside it

parts.note: the Pope is head of the Catholic Church
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A pontiff holding Mass ahead of two Latin-speaking villages of ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two in Latin' is Roman numeral II; 'mass' is not the church service but M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town buried by Vesuvius in AD 79 is an ancient settlement, a community of long ago.

clue.text: Bar return of vessels

indicators.note: return means going back, so the word for vessels is read backwards

parts.note: pots are vessels for holding things

explanation.surface: A pub asking for its glasses back.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bar something is to prevent or block it.

clue.text: Heap in hole, restricted

indicators.note: restricted means curtailed, so the last letter of the hole word is cut

parts.note: a crater is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: A pile of rubble dumped in a pit with limited access.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted' cuts the final letter from CRATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: an old, battered car is a heap or banger, also called a crate.

clue.text: Warriors in football team, say, surrounding lawmaker

indicators.note: surrounding means the team's figure goes round the lawmaker

parts.note: a football side has eleven players, written 11 and taken as the letters II
an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws

explanation.surface: Fighters in a football squad encircle a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: An impi is a Zulu regiment; a football team is an eleven, written 11 and read as II.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zulu fighting regiment is a body of warriors.

clue.text: Imperial figure, part of fine royalty

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An emperor is described as part of a splendid royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor of the first century was an imperial ruler.

clue.text: Item that's cut, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is given by its sound

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut

explanation.surface: An object that has been trimmed, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item' looks like a thing; here it is a couple, as in 'they're an item'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: two people who are 'an item' are a romantic couple, a twosome.

clue.text: Consumption perhaps less in ground with fifty inside

indicators.note: inside says the numeral is placed within the rearranged letters
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Eating less, with fifty of something inside, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' gives ILNESS, and 'inside' puts L within it. Consumption is an old name for tuberculosis, not eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumption, the old name for tuberculosis, is an example of a disease.

clue.text: Elevated land recently seen in French city

indicators.note: seen in means found inside, so the word for recently sits within the city's name

parts.note: Pau is a city in south-west France
lately or late means recently

explanation.surface: High ground recently spotted in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a raised area of fairly flat land is a tableland or upland.

clue.text: Inaction reveals varied activity abandoned in UK

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doing nothing shows a range of pursuits that Britain gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: Compulsory peacetime military service ended in Britain in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscription into the armed forces was a duty in Britain until it was phased out around 1960.
